text:
Alex M: Quick follow-up from the RFC — thinking about hybrid routing: prefer low-latency endpoints but degrade to cheaper ones when cost budgets hit. How do folks feel about making 'cost' a soft signal vs hard filter?
Maria P: soft signal seems safer. hard filters risk dropping to slow/failed endpoints under transient spikes. we need graceful weight shifts.
Chris L: Agree. Also worried about evaluation perf if policies are complex per-request. We can't add 2-3ms p95 just to evaluate routing.
Alex M: Good point. Proposal: compile policies to a decision DAG at deploy-time. runtime = traverse small DAG + metric lookups. keeps runtime O(depth).
Taylan: +1 to compile step. Also we should precompute weight buckets per tenant so we can sample cheap paths without per-request expensive math.
Jin W: For telemetry, emit: chosen_variant, expected_cost_delta, estimated_latency. that helps debugging / console.
Maria P: Another tradeoff: where to store state for cost budgets? per-tenant in-memory counters vs global aggregator. in-memory is fast but loses cross-instance coordination.
Chris L: Could do soft-local budgets with periodic global reconciliation. local ensures low-latency decisions, global avoids abuse.
Alex M: Example policy idea:
```
policy {
  priority: latency
  fallback: cost_weighted
  budget_window: 1h
  max_overspend: 5%
}
```
This compiles to: try low-latency pool until local_budget_exhausted -> pick weighted cheapest.
Taylan: For implementation, lookups we need: pool_latency(p), pool_cost(p), tenant_budget(t). keep them in LRU caches with 50ms TTL.
Chris L: Benchmarks? I ran a prototype: decision DAG traversal + cache lookups ~ 120us median, 700us p99 under load. acceptable.
Alex M: Nice. Can we get p99 < 1ms across real traffic? if not, maybe we only evaluate full policy on requests flagged as 'sensitive' and use static default for low-sensitivity.
Maria P: Also need admin override endpoints so SRE can force fallback to known good pool during incidents.
Jin W: UI: show a timeline of budget consumption and policy hits per-tenant. Expose per-route debug toggle to log decision path.
Alex M: Ops question — how to do canary for policy code? We should rollout compiled DAGs across a subset of hosts and compare decisions vs old algorithm.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for routing-policy-dag v2 on pool infra (10% hosts) :rocket:
Taylan: Let's also include a safety net: if evaluation latency exceeds threshold or caches miss heavily, fallback to default routing (least-latency historical).
Chris L: Agree. Also add unit tests that verify monotonicity: if latency improves, priority picks that pool; if cost drops 50%, weight adjusts.
Alex M: Next steps: draft compile spec and a small prototype for tenant-local budget store + reconciliation routine. I'll open RFC follow-up doc. @Taylan @Chris can you pair on prototype?
Taylan: Yep. I'll sync with Chris tomorrow.
Chris L: Count me in.
Maria P: I'll sketch the console telemetry counters.
Alex M: Thanks all. I'll drop the RFC follow-up link once it's up.
